tb21_profile.skill: Build a large legacy C++ ML framework from a git clone with the right feature flags (CPU-only) and dependencies, then drive its example scripts to train a CNN and read accuracy out of the log
tb21_profile.domain: Deep learning frameworks (Caffe/CNN/CIFAR-10), C++/CMake/Makefile.config builds, protobuf-style solver configs
tb21_profile.task_form: build-from-source plus configure-and-run-a-training-job until a numeric accuracy target is met

TMax-15K.reason: Fix a C++ classifier's training code, compile it with g++ and run it so it emits Test Accuracy - compile-then-train-then-read-accuracy, same loop.
Repair a vendored CMakeLists C++ standard so the library builds, then implement a neural-net forward pass in C++ - build fix plus net semantics.
Training run diverges to NaN; must debug the pipeline until training actually completes without touching lr, seed, epochs or architecture.
Recover exact architecture hyperparameters, train, and be graded on held-out accuracy - same architecture-config-then-accuracy-target structure.
Write and compile a C classifier, cross-validate it and print average validation accuracy; native-code training with a metric to hit.
Model is judged on a hidden test set and must exceed a fixed accuracy floor, exactly like the >45% / within-5% gate here.
Iterate the data-prep script, re-running the evaluator until reported ACCURACY clears a threshold - same run-inspect-metric-retry loop.
Fix a broken training pipeline and then meet a performance budget; combines correctness of training with a measured target.
Run a tracked training job and write the exact computed test accuracy to a file; only the report-the-metric step transfers.
Track down a bug in a training script by running it and reading its output; debugging-a-training-run but pure Python sklearn.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Clone source, build with the cmake flags a spec file dictates, install, then compile and run a smoke test and log its full output.
Set up the env, download the four MNIST data files, run the example classification script and save the whole run output.
Clone an image-classification library, build an env for it, fetch MNIST and run its example - clone-install-fetch-data-run, same chain.
Same sds-mnist setup: venv, deps, download the dataset files, supply the missing config, run the classifier.
A JSON config file specifies a network architecture that must be materialised and profiled - the solver/net-prototxt idea in Python.
Clone a C library repo, build it from source and install system-wide before anything downstream can run.
Fit a classification pipeline with a controlled random seed and produce predictions; trains a model but no build and no accuracy gate.
Run a provided training workflow, then serve the model and collect predictions; mostly workflow driving, not training control.
Train a classification model on a tabular dataset after inspecting the workspace; shallow sklearn pipeline, no native build.
Run a three-stage pipeline whose first stage trains SVR models from provided scripts; driving someone else's training code.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Compile an OpenCV binding from source with precompiled artifacts disabled, load YOLOv4 weights and run inference - build-flag wrangling plus a CNN.
Build and install a scientific C++ solver from source, then run a supplied model file and capture all stdout/stderr to a result file.
Use the libsvm source tree to split heart_scale, train a classifier and evaluate it - train-with-a-C++-toolkit and report accuracy.
Clone a machine-learning C++ library, init submodules and build it with CMake with tests enabled; same build-an-ML-lib-from-git job.
Train an SVM with LIBSVM on a train/validation split and produce model plus predictions files; training-and-evaluating with a C toolkit.
Clone two scientific packages and build them from source into a local prefix; dependency-ordered source builds.
Install an MNIST image-similarity library from GitHub and run its example classification workflow end to end.
Provision a deep-learning environment (CUDA/cuDNN/torch) on a pinned base - the dependency-stack half of getting Caffe to build.
Install CPU-only PyTorch and then the cloned package - the same deliberately-CPU-only deep-learning install constraint.
Build MNIST datasets from an example project's dataset.yaml; only the prepare-the-example-dataset step overlaps.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: c2_xavier_fill / c2_msra_fill weight init for conv and linear layers - literally the Caffe2 initialisation scheme a CNN trains under.
Model statistics over a conv net; requires reasoning about layer shapes and parameter counts the way a net definition does.
Checkpointer.load fails to restore weights - the same save/restore-a-trained-model concern as the .caffemodel snapshot.
PeriodicCheckpointer and CfgNode bugs: iteration-based snapshotting and config merging, the solver.prototxt machinery in Python.
CfgNode computed-attribute handling - config-file semantics for a training framework, no training run involved.
SqueezeExcitation block behaves wrongly; requires reading a CNN module's forward path carefully.
FLOP counting for matmul in a traced net; layer-level arithmetic of a conv/fc network.
HistoryBuffer of training metrics is broken - the smoothed loss/accuracy bookkeeping you read out of a training log.
giou_loss computes the wrong value; loss-function correctness in a vision training stack.
Module hierarchy printed in reverse; only the inspect-a-network-structure habit transfers.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Loss tracker is lost when a model is compiled more than once - exactly the compile/solver-state confusion that breaks a training run.
ValueError raised inside the loss during actual training; requires reasoning about a real training loop, not just an API.
Build/compile/fit path of a model with a preprocessing layer - the layer-configuration-affects-training relationship.
CNN tiling/padding removal produces an empty array; conv-net spatial bookkeeping of exactly the CIFAR-sized kind.
Training entrypoint crashes on a None; debugging a deep-learning framework's training path.
Dataset iteration scheme is exhausted after one epoch - epoch/batch iteration semantics of a data layer.
Main training loop fails getting its epoch iterator; same data-feeding-into-a-training-loop territory.
Model compile under a distribution strategy; framework-level training configuration, no build or metric target.
Multi-input model compiled with a loss behaves wrongly; ordinary DL-framework debugging.
Pipelines are not given a random_state, so runs are irreproducible - the seeding discipline a graded training run needs.

Compile an OpenCV binding from source with precompiled artifacts disabled, then run a YOLOv4 CNN on a test image.
Compile a C++ training program and run it so it prints Test Accuracy; native-code training with a metric to verify.
Set up the environment, download the dataset files and run the example classifier, saving the full run output.
Split a dataset, train an SVM with the libsvm source tree and evaluate it - train-and-measure with a C++ toolkit.
Build and install a scientific C++ package from source, then run a supplied model and capture all output to a file.
Fix a vendored CMakeLists so the C++ dependency builds, then implement the network's forward pass by hand.
Clone a machine-learning C++ library with submodules and build it with CMake and tests enabled.
Training diverges to NaN and must be made to converge without touching lr, seed, epochs or architecture.
Caffe2-style conv weight initialisation (c2_msra_fill/c2_xavier_fill) - the initialisation a CIFAR CNN's accuracy depends on.

notes: No corpus contains Caffe, CIFAR-10, prototxt or CPU_ONLY - a search over all 56k instructions returned three irrelevant hits for 'convolutional'. So nothing matches both halves of this task; I ranked candidates that hit one half well (build-a-C/C++-project-from-source-with-flags, or train-a-model-to-an-accuracy-target) over Python ML-pipeline chores that merely share the word 'training'. The retrieval shortlist for TMax and RTS was almost entirely sklearn ETL/'data leakage' pipelines - high lexical overlap on 'machine learning', near-zero transfer to a framework build; I demoted essentially all of them. SWE-Smith's only deep-learning repo is fvcore, so its ten are all fvcore; SWE-Rebench's are keras/opennmt/fuel. Both are honest 2-3s.
